Full text, all ~67.8k clean chars in five windows incl. Appendices A–F and Tables 6–10. **Substance:** ten controlled tasks (Math digits, Math words, GSM-Plus, Spell-m, Spell-mi, Math-Parse, Ling-Parse, Ling-SV, Ling-GA, Ling-HJ) crossed with five models; EAP-IG circuit extraction over five integrated-gradient steps under three edge boundaries (top 2.5%, top 5%, adaptive to self-faithfulness 0.85); IoU for structure and a **mask-transfer faithfulness** for function (task A's clean input, task A's own corrupted activations patched into every edge outside circuit B, recovered fraction of the clean-corrupted gap, then divided by A's self-faithfulness); Ward clustering of the transfer-profile rows with ARI and cophenetic agreement across the ten model pairs. **Results:** arithmetic/linguistic dissociation in every model and boundary, sharper under the adaptive definition; digits and number words produce similar circuits to each other and unlike the spelling circuits, so vocabulary is not the determinant; the same expressions asked to be spelled out rather than computed switch their circuit's transfer profile; and the purpose-built parsing pair is the *most* dissociated case in the suite (near-zero both directions in most models). Cross-model clustering agreement runs ~0.45–0.63 mean ARI, with Llama-3.1-8B alone at cophenetic 0.45–0.59 against 0.95–0.98 among Qwen3-4B/Qwen3-8B/Gemma-2-2B. **Why relevance 3:** the cross-application protocol is the cheapest specificity test the folder lacked — it prices edges by what they do rather than by whether they are shared — and the paper's own deliberately-matched pair is the case that refutes the prior a reader would bring to it.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 218): **Overlap and substitutability are different measurements and can point in opposite directions on the same pair of circuits, so any claim that structure X is specific to behaviour Y needs the cross-application matrix and not an IoU number — here the arithmetic and sentence-parsing circuits are the pair the authors built to *maximise* structural similarity, and while their edge overlap is reported only as colour on a heatmap their cross-transfer is near zero in both directions (Math-Parse recovers 0.05 of Spell-m and 0.04 of Ling-Parse on Llama; 0.03 and 0.16 on Qwen3-4B), so two circuits can be near-substitutes for their own targets and useless for each other's.**
Two habits follow from the paper's own arithmetic. The transferable object should be the *mask*, never the activations: hold the target task's clean and corrupted runs fixed and swap only which edges are allowed to carry clean signal, which is what makes the resulting score a statement about the circuit's sufficiency rather than about how similar two datasets were. And the matrix should be published raw, because the paper's normalisation hides its own strongest evidence — dividing each column by the target's self-faithfulness produces diagonal cells above 1.0 (Llama's agreement circuit at 1.60, Gemma's sentence-parsing circuit at 1.26, Gemma's inverse-spelling circuit reaching 1.14 into sentence parsing, above its own 0.97 self-score) which the text acknowledges as small-baseline amplification but which no reader can undo without the baseline-normalised tables in the appendix. For our battery the rule is: report the recovered fraction of the clean-corrupted gap, report the target's self-value beside it, and cap the normalisation at the self-value rather than trusting it as a denominator. (arxiv-2610.27790, core/arxiv-2403.17806, arxiv-2606.16939)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 218): **A control task built specifically to give a hypothesis its best chance can end up the strongest evidence against it, and that inversion is worth designing for rather than being surprised by — the authors construct an operator-precedence task and a sentence head-word task with deliberately parallel recursive structure precisely because the linguistic literature reports cross-domain interaction there, and it is that pair, not the easy arithmetic-versus-agreement contrast, that dissociates most cleanly, to near-zero transfer in both directions across most of the five models while each circuit still recovers a decent share of its own target.**
The methodological point generalises to every "we built a matched pair" claim in this folder: the matched pair's result is the load-bearing one, so it should be pre-registered as a falsifier with a stated threshold rather than narrated after the fact as one of several findings. A second, quieter result has the same shape — surface form turns out not to fix the circuit (digits and number words give similar circuits on Llama at 0.58 diagonal with 0.48 transfer between them, and on Qwen3-8B both land near 0.55–0.60 against the calculation and word-problem targets while the spelling circuits sit at 0.12–0.24 there) but the *instruction* does, which means the variable that had to be controlled was the one the authors thought of as a nuisance (vocabulary) while the one that carries the effect (what the task asks for) was the one they varied deliberately. Write the nuisance variables down and then check which one actually moves the answer; here it was not the one on the checklist. (arxiv-2610.27790, arxiv-2611.01513, arxiv-2610.37157)

- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 218): **Cross-model agreement should be reported per model, because a mean over five models can describe none of them — the appendix gives cophenetic correlations of 0.95–0.98 among Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2-2B while Llama-3.1-8B sits at 0.45–0.59 against every other model and Qwen3-1.7B sits intermediate at 0.70–0.76, so the paper's "moderate overall agreement" (mean ARI 0.45–0.63 depending on the cut level) is an average of a tight cluster and one outlier, and the authors note that clustering similarity tracks neither family nor parameter count.**
The concrete consequence for a stability or replication claim of ours: the summary statistic to publish is the sorted list of pairwise agreements with the model names attached, plus the count of pairs below any threshold we would act on, and the cut level has to be fixed in advance because ARI here ranges from 0.452 at four clusters to 0.628 at two on the same dendrograms. This is the same failure shape as the folder's pooled-agreement and pooled-separation findings — a single number whose denominator includes regions where everything passes — arriving on the cross-model axis, and it pairs with the standing rule that a stability claim needs an independently-trained arm rather than a re-scoring of existing runs. (arxiv-2610.27790, arxiv-2608.20134, arxiv-2606.02061)

- Done 2026-11-16 (entry 241): `arxiv-2611.18274` — Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering (Nima Eshraghi, Lovedeep Gondara, Sagarika Suresh, Xiaotong Xu, Jithin Pradeep, Fanny Chevalier — Vanguard / University of Toronto; arXiv:2611.18274v1, 2026-11-13, CC BY 4.0). Full text, all ~108.5k clean chars in six windows. **Framing:** steering recast as **budgeted per-token allocation** — fix the steered-token fraction p, fix direction v and magnitude α, and the gate sequence m_{1:T} is the only free variable, so at matched p every method comparison is a controlled ablation. Direction built from top-k SAE feature differentials between a target and neutral corpus; a task-agnostic probe `u = sign(α)v` makes `⟨h_t,u⟩` monotone in target alignment for both suppression and elicitation. **Two gates:** **CFP** memoryless, fires when `⟨h_t,u⟩ ≤ τ` with τ calibrated to p, one dot product per token, and is exactly the budget-calibrated form of feature-triggered conditional steering; **CLABS** standardises the projection, sets error `e_t = s⋆ − ŝ_t` and a **leaky integral** `ē_t` (EWMA, memory ~1/β), then samples `m_t ~ Bernoulli(clip(p₀ + κ_p e_t + κ_i ē_t))` with p₀ calibrated to the budget — no rollouts, no backtracking, no learned scorer, overhead ~1e-6 of a forward pass. **Theory:** Assumption 1 is a first-order steering-response model `ŝ_{t+1} = φŝ_t + (1−φ)β₀ + g m_t + η_t`; the controller state follows a 2×2 linear recursion with `a = φ − gκ_p`, and Theorem 1's sufficient condition for ρ(A)<1 is `0 ≤ a < 1` and `0 ≤ gκ_i < (2−β)(1+a)/β`, yielding geometric convergence of the mean, asymptotic variance `≤ c(A)σ̄²`, and time-averaged squared error `O(1/T)+O(σ̄²)`; Corollary 1 gives `e_ss = N/(1−φ+g(κ_p+κ_i))` and so `|e_ss|` non-increasing in κ_i; Remark 1 makes the leaky integral's cost explicit with a positive floor on `|e_ss|` — bounded memory buys a reduced but nonzero offset. **Results:** Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B, one mid-network layer, three targets (RealToxicityPrompts detoxification, GoEmotions fear and sadness elicitation), AlpacaEval for competence, three seeds, three corrections applied identically to every method. CFP and CLABS get the largest behavioral shift among budgeted gates on all six panels, **2–3× the entropy gates and random control at the smallest budgets**, converging with them as p→1; CLABS recovers **89–92%** of the Full-steer shift on emotion targets at moderate budget. They are the **only gates preferred to No-steer at every budget under both judges** (gpt-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6) on AlpacaEval, with PPL 23–28 vs 41.2 for Full-steer at p=1.0 and distinct-2 ~0.86–0.91 vs 0.68. **Ablation (Table 3, p=0.5):** toxicity reduction open-loop 0.12 → I-only 0.15 → P-only 0.21 → PI 0.24, perplexity 9.8 → 9.0 → 8.9 → 8.6, I-only widest seed variance. **Budget honesty:** realized rates within 0.04 of nominal for all methods, CFP/CLABS ranges inside STS's, ranking unchanged at realized rates. **Negatives the paper prints itself:** the authors' own SRE baseline (steer where the SAE reconstructs faithfully) is mid-pack rather than competitive, and they explicitly do *not* reproduce SIA — they extract its selection signals (predictive entropy, entropy rise) as single-pass gates, so SIA's numbers here are not SIA's. **Limitations:** two open base models, one layer, one direction, English, three classifier-scorable targets, no human eval, and the stability result is a *linearisation around the interior operating point*, explicitly not a worst-case guarantee. **Why relevance 3:** it isolates an axis the folder has discussed only as a side condition, and supplies the guardrail — the gain box — that turns "pick a steering strength" into something that can be refused in advance rather than discovered as oscillation.
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **When the intervention budget is fixed, allocation stops being a nuisance variable and becomes the treatment — and the fraction of tokens steered turns out to be a better first-class knob than the magnitude, because at matched realized budgets the choice of *which* tokens to steer moves behavior by 2–3× at p ≤ 0.2 while the methods converge as p → 1 (Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B, three targets, both judges).**
Concretely, this reframes a design decision the folder has been making implicitly: `arxiv-2611.04757` asked whether a steering edit should depend on the input and `arxiv-2611.04349` argued for sparse internal control, but neither held cost constant, so "sparser is better" and "the direction is better" could not be separated. Fixing p and holding v and α fixed does separate them, and the result is that the *informed* gates beat random Bernoulli(p) gating at the same spend while an entropy-based gate — a plausible need signal — falls furthest behind precisely when the budget is scarce. The transferable rule: publish steering results as efficacy *at a stated intervention ratio*, with the random gate at matched realized spend as the mandatory floor, and treat any comparison that varies density and strength together as unreported. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2611.04757, arxiv-2611.04349)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **A stability certificate is worth more than an effect size when the controller reads its own output, because the failure mode is oscillation rather than weakness — and the certificate here is closed-form in quantities you can estimate, which is what makes it usable: stability holds iff `0 ≤ φ − gκ_p < 1` and `0 ≤ gκ_i < (2−β)(1+a)/β`, so the proportional gain is capped by activation persistence and the integral gain by the memory length, and the same box that guarantees convergence also bounds how much the integral term can help, giving `|e_ss| > 0` for every admissible gain.**
Two consequences. First, a closed loop needs a stated certificate with its operating assumptions printed beside it — here Assumption 1's linearisation holds only where the calibrated budget keeps the gating probability off its clip bounds, which the authors say plainly rather than burying in an appendix. Second, the leaky integral is a deliberate downgrade from exact tracking: an EWMA of the error trades offset for bounded memory, so the honest reporting of a PI controller in this setting includes the residual steady-state offset and its floor, not just the variance bound. The same discipline applies to any adaptive probe, adaptive threshold, or budgeted patrol of ours that consumes its own output as input: name the quantity that persists between steps, state the region where the response is linear enough for the analysis to apply, and refuse gains outside the box. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2610.27393, arxiv-2611.12206)
- Pattern 2026-11-16 (run 219): **Fluency and efficacy are reported together at a matched budget or the comparison is uninterpretable — the same method that looks best on behavioral shift at p=0.2 can be worst on both axes once the quality cost is priced in, since a light touch preserves utility while barely moving the target, and the paper's own table shows an entropy gate winning a single AlpacaEval cell that its efficacy curve contradicts.**
The authors' handling is the template: every gate is compared at the same realized rate (within 0.04 of nominal, with the random gate's sampling spread as the reference band), the ranking is re-read at realized rather than nominal rates, and instruction-following is reported under two independent judges so a lone favourable cell can be checked against the other. For the folder this closes a loop with the objective-inflation and pooled-agreement findings — a metric that can be won by doing less, reported without the cost dimension, is a denominator problem. The rule to carry: any controlled-generation result should print efficacy, quality, and spend together in one row, and a single-best-cell claim must come with its contradicting curve. (arxiv-2611.18274, arxiv-2611.11035, arxiv-2611.18514)

Full text, 132,082 clean chars; **Tables 2–5, 7, 8 and 16–19 populated and quoted**, abstract intact, **Tables 9–15 and most inline numerals stripped by the HTML build** and therefore described rather than quoted; figures via captions only. **Substance:** ConfabQA (784 items = 4 domains × 3 categories, the obscure pre-cutoff cell breaking the cutoff/correctness confound) plus 800-item PopQA and TriviaQA samples, scored three-way by a same-model judge calibrated against a web-search annotator over all 784 items and a second annotator on a stratified sample; per-layer linear probes (standardise → PCA(16) → logistic regression, 5-fold CV) on the last-prompt-position prefill state of Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma 2 2B, Llama 3.2 3B and a Qwen3-4B within-family control, every probe scored as Δ against a four-rung prompt-feature ladder plus a label-permutation null and a balanced-subsample bootstrap; logit-lens vocabulary of the recovered direction; one-shot forward-hook pushes at the post-block residual swept in units of the state norm, with three norm-matched random directions, a shuffled-label probe, a directly optimised direction, a prefix-forcing arm and a native pre-norm probe refit as controls; SAE decomposition against Qwen-Scope TopK features with a three-view convergent ranking and a causal test of the single surviving opener feature; and a no-refit cross-dataset transfer matrix. **Results:** 235 correct / 147 refusal / 402 wrong (30.0% / 18.8% / 51.3%), accuracy 62.2% well-known vs 33.3% obscure vs 19.5% post-cutoff, all refusals post-cutoff; correctness adds ≤2.4 pp over the +category baseline (0.824 vs 0.800) and the disconfounded within-stratum margins are consistent with zero under the bootstrap, while refusal-vs-wrong clears TF-IDF by +7.4 / +16.3 / +2.2 pp (82.0 / 67.6 / 93.6 baselines) on Qwen/Gemma/Llama; the lens puts "as" first with the Chinese variants at ranks 2–3 and "there" at rank 11; pushes flip the first token to refusal openers from a sub-norm dose but only about one third survive as judged refusals, and forcing "As" with no activation edit yields the same rate; three recovery routes 50–81° apart all work, the optimised vector most dose-efficiently and the SAE feature at roughly half the probe's dose; on PopQA the Llama correctness probe reaches 82.37% vs 61.61% and on TriviaQA 74.23% vs 56.52% with ranges excluding zero, Qwen3-4B lands at Qwen3-1.7B's level, and the refusal channel accounts for about a sixth of it. **Commit:** 249 is a multiple of three, so this run batches at its close.
